   |              B|    Out  meaning     to the  end  or  completely                                                         |
                        Sometimes  out in phrasal verbs gives an idea of completing or doing something to the end.
                           | sorted out my room on Sunday. [arranged things that were untidy]
                           | cleared out [made tidy by removing unwanted things] all my wardrobes and threw away all my
                          worn-out  shoes. [adjective: used so much that they had become damaged, from the verb wear out]
                          Unfortunately, I’d run out of furniture polish, so | couldn’t do any polishing, but I’ll do that next
                          weekend.  [there was none left because it had all been used]
